scores.concept: ONE ISLAND, ONE TAP — the void's window
scores.notes: USABILITY 3: picture-pips are right for a non-reader and the locked-pip wiggle with no refusal text/sound is the best locked-state handling of the three, but there is NO fail-forward inside a world — a six-year-old stuck on pip 3 LANDMARK (worlds 2-5 cross the hero threshold only in the finale surge, prototype3d.ts:1553-1555; whale needs R 16.22 > LAW_TOP 12, :9745) stares at the same green dot forever; BY MYSELF is buried in the #settings sheet; 'LEVEL 7 OF 30' is printed on the menu. FIRST-SECOND 4: the cleanest window of the three (only the season pennant intrudes) and the void is the subject with the world's moving thing behind him — the most literal answer to 'make the splash alive'. FLOW 3: menu->PLAY is one tap, but the level loop is CONTINUE -> menu -> pip hop -> PLAY, i.e. two taps per level and a cut into the descent every time; the pip hop is a nice reward but it is the only concept that makes the child pay a tap for it. IDENTITY 3: creature behaviour is thin (cruise + blink + chomp + pupils on the camera) and the chrome is Hole.io's — tab hues #3d7bff/#4c3cbe/#ff9a2e and pip colours lifted verbatim from recon.md:249-252; worst of all the pips are platform EMOJI (🍔🧺👑🌍 + heroCue glyphs :1543-1664), which render as Noto in the Chromium lookbook and Apple glyphs on the phone and read as a web page, not this game's painted art (index.html:994 already records 'system emoji standing in for the art' as a past mistake). PERF 3: closest orbit radius (28) but a FULL 360° turn around a rim stage sweeps the frustum across the whole plateau every 45 s — the 4,694-draw-call class (:10496-10500) is in the orbit, not out of it; the ≤1,400 bar will fail on the inward half unless the stage is inside the island. BUILD 3: 15.5 days with a 6-row MENU_STAGE table, void warp to stage, a 3-day probe migration; sane order (measure first). OWNER 5: every decision honoured (five goals, board retired, first-touch clock, win-on-spot, 3 tabs, moving water actually in the Maple frame via the waterfall lip).

scores.concept: Splash Alive — the living island menu with the five-bite ladder
scores.notes: USABILITY 4: fail-forward after three misses (the in-world 'never a wall' of unlocks.ts:5-26), 'NOT YET' with the counter frozen and coins still paid, icons inside the pips, solo chip on the goal line greyed on level 4, no 1-30 on the menu; loses a point because the locked-pip response is a READING line ('FINISH LEVEL 2 FIRST') and the goal line itself is text a six-year-old cannot read — the scared blink is the only non-text cue. FIRST-SECOND 3: the 49% window is cluttered — logo lockup over the sky, world plate bottom-left, season chip, status strip all inside the diorama band — so the first second is the void plus four pieces of chrome, and the 3-layer logo type over a moving sky is exactly the 'UI moves with the world' read recon.md:629 forbids; also parking the void '9 units in front of the hero' puts him inside Skylark's r18 whale. FLOW 4: one tap; CONTINUE goes straight into the next pip via resetMatch (no menu round-trip), PLAY makes him 'hungry' for the descent, per-level camera nudge (L3 toward the hero, L4 the family visible) is the smartest use of the diorama; loses a point because a chaining child never sees the menu's ladder — the pip lights only on #endPips. IDENTITY 4: the richest creature vocabulary (cruise/smug/hungry/scared through the rig API void3d.ts:54-75, pointer-tracked pupils, chomp on tap), goal lines in each world's voice, SCRAPBOOK-with-chapters instead of a skins tab, season lights a lantern in the world, and the key art moves to the boot cover so the picture literally becomes the moving window — but the chrome is Hole.io's measured proportions and hues (45/49, #4c3cbe, blue/violet/orange) and the hero pip is an emoji. PERF 4: the most credible frame — 22-unit camera, ±6° pendulum (never the far plateau), shadows left where the renderer has them, DPR 1.3, bloom off, menu rung applied before the first animate(), ratio bar ≤1.15 plus draw calls ≤1.3x in-match, crowdGate 138, visibilitychange stop, 45 s idle half-rate; missing only the first-toggle recompile pre-warm and a menu-only degrade ladder. BUILD 4: 13.5 days, streams 2-4 parallel after a half-day baseline, the per-level nudge and the lantern emissive are the only extras. OWNER 5: every decision honoured; the recon numbers the owner measured himself are hit to the pixel.

scores.concept: LIVING SPLASH — the key art rendered live, five pips under it, one tap to play
scores.notes: USABILITY 3: pips are 36 px (current 46) — under the 44 pt tap minimum for a six-year-old and smaller than the 44/57 the owner measured; pips are numerals with no goal picture, so the goal lives only in a 16 px reading line; fail-forward exists but announces itself in text ('YOU CAN SKIP AHEAD'); the scripted gaze-up and 14 s chomp beats are the best zero-input delight of the three. FIRST-SECOND 4: the feathered OVAL window is the strongest single image on the table — the island floats in our cosmos exactly as the key art does, the void at real scale looks UP at the landmark, the logo sits in its own band and nothing but the season pill touches the window; loses a point because Maple's azimuth is chosen to keep the waterfall OUT of frame, so the first world a child sees has no moving water at all (pond/river are baked, island.ts:3119-3249) until an optional stream 5. FLOW 4: one tap, CONTINUE into the next level without a reload, and the ONLY concept that handles menu re-entry (900 ms ease from the match camera to the parked orbit) and the #daily condition (:7967 keys on menuEl.style.display); docked for the self-contradiction on LANDMARK (a 'stolen' fail state AND rival exclusion 'as the fix'). IDENTITY 5: own palette (the game's #33175e->#0d0821 cosmos and star dots, teal/violet/plum tabs) instead of Hole.io's slab and hues, no emoji anywhere on the menu, the giant poster mouth explicitly NOT reproduced ('the void stays his real size, a creature in the scene'), the family named as a family on level 4, copy is 'EAT THE TOWN HALL' never 'consume x items', the poster wall kept as the sell for the NEXT world while the window is always THIS world with the void in it. PERF 3: the widest frame (58 units, height 24, ±12° swing, bar ≤1.6x ≈ 2,000 draws) is the expensive one and the concept says so; the compensations are the best on the table (menu-only three-step degrade never touching qLevel, renderer.compile pre-warm for the first shadow toggle per AUDIT-2026-08-23.md:316, visibility gate, 60 s / 5 min idle tiers) but they are a ladder for a cost the framing created. BUILD 3: 16.5 days, most surface — oval mask, degrade ladder, re-parenting #trophies/#topvoids overlays into #book, daily rewrite, the guards. OWNER 3: departs from the numbers the owner measured (ground hue, pip sizes, ground share), drops moving water from the Maple window on purpose after he asked for 'moving water', and prints 'LEVEL 2 OF 5' on the world chip.

winner: Splash Alive — the living island menu with the five-bite ladder
grafts_from_runners_up: From LIVING SPLASH: take the feathered OVAL window and the game's own cosmos ground (#33175e -> #1c0f3d -> #0d0821 with the ::before star dots, index.html:888-896) in place of the Hole.io slab #4c3cbe, and own the three tab hues (bright versions of teal/violet/plum, each ≥ deltaE 15 apart and ≥ 4.5:1 under its label) — keep the 45/49 proportions the owner measured, drop his competitor's paint.

From LIVING SPLASH: move the logo, world plate and status strip OUT of the window into their own bands (identity band above, pips below); the only thing allowed inside the 49% is the world, the void and the season pill at the top edge — the window must read as one uncluttered picture in the first second.

From LIVING SPLASH: the 900 ms camera ease from the match position to the parked orbit on HOME/quit (single lerp on camera.position, not camFollow), and the rewrite of the #daily raise condition (prototype3d.ts:7967) to key on body.menu instead of menuEl.style.display — both are correctness holes in the winner as written.

From LIVING SPLASH: the menu-only degrade ladder (menuRung in __menuState, never written to qLevel: DPR 1.0 -> shadows off via the intro toggle :10505-10509 -> frozen orbit at half rate with dt doubled into island.update), the renderer.compile() pre-warm so the first shadow toggle's recompile (docs/AUDIT-2026-08-23.md:316) never lands on a menu frame, and the two idle tiers (60 s half-rate, 5 min quarter-rate) on top of the winner's visibilitychange stop.

From LIVING SPLASH: the scripted zero-input beats — gaze UP at the landmark every 6-9 s for 1.4 s via lookX/lookY (void3d.ts:2340-2347) and one chomp(0.6) every ~14 s preceded by 0.8 s of 'hungry' — so the creature is alive before the child touches anything, and the key-art relationship (void below, island above, looking up) is kept in the framing.

From ONE ISLAND: the per-world MENU_STAGE idea that puts the world's MOVING thing in frame for levels 1/2/5 (Maple waterfall lip + balloon, island.ts:3812-3838/:8857; Pirate bay swell :3880-3931; Powder skaters life.ts:4718; Skylark launch circle), with the winner's per-level nudge swinging to the hero landmark only on L3/L4 — never author a Maple stage with no water in it.

From ONE ISLAND: the locked-pip response is a 200 ms wiggle + padlock jiggle + one low pop and NO text — replace the winner's 'FINISH LEVEL 2 FIRST' reading line with that plus the scared blink; likewise the fail-forward opening should be shown (the next pip's padlock pops off on the end card) not announced in words.

From ONE ISLAND: UI holds still — drop the declared PLAY breathe and the current-pip ring pulse so qa/menu.mjs bar 3 is a flat zero after settle (recon.md:629); the world moves, the buttons do not; and the shorter 20 s idle threshold before half-rate rendering.

From ONE ISLAND: the season chip as a pennant with a paintWorldCard poster thumb and a DATE (never a countdown) rather than a bare pill, and the explicit rule that solo applies to goals 1/2/3/5 and never to goal 4 (state it to the owner as a decision, not 'to confirm').
what_all_three_missed: ICONS ARE NOT THE GAME'S ART: all three draw the pips, the goal line and the #goal HUD with platform emoji (heroCue glyphs prototype3d.ts:1543-1664; 🍔🧺👑🌍) — Chromium renders Noto in qa/lookbook, iOS renders Apple glyphs, and index.html:994 already records 'system emoji standing in for the art' as a shipped mistake. The one-game answer is to render the actual props (town hall, Royal Mariner, stadium, bathhouse, lodge, whale, a car, a house, a snack) to sprites with the existing ASSETVIEW camera branch (:10488-10490) at build time and use THOSE as pip and HUD icons; nobody proposed it.

THE MENU STILL WAITS FOR THE WORLD: createIsland is a top-level await (:1733) and the boot cover (#loadScr z60, index.html:2143) is released only by the first rendered frame (:10931-10935), so on every launch the child sees a cover for the whole 'handful of seconds' build and only then the menu. None of the three show the menu chrome immediately with the painted splash_hero.webp (index.html:909-912) sitting in the window and cross-fade it to the live world when the island is ready — which is the literal 'make our splash image alive' and would cut perceived time-to-PLAY to under a second. Splash Alive's boot-cover trick gets closest but still holds the cover.

NO SOUND FOR THE DIORAMA: 'alive' is half audio and all three change nothing (menu.mp3 on menuCh, audio3d.ts:432-440). Nobody decides whether the window carries the world's ambience (waterfall hiss, bay, crowd murmur, the void's chomp) under or instead of the menu theme, nor how the first tap on the void (the unlock gesture, audio3d.ts:282-324) sounds when nothing can play before it — the first chomp of every session is silent as designed and no one noticed.

BIG MOTION / REDUCED MOTION IS IGNORED: the game has a BIG MOTION switch (index.html:1999, :2034; reduceMotion() in prototype3d.ts:7734/:8107; voidMotion in src/proto3d/fx.ts:51 with a prefers-reduced-motion query at :46). None of the three gate the orbit/pendulum, the pip pulses or the PLAY breathe on it; a menu that moves for minutes must honour the one accessibility toggle the owner already shipped.

ONLY ONE VIEWPORT: every band table is authored to 430x932 and nothing says what collapses on a 393x700-class phone (firstframe.mjs measured there, and it already saw canvas bleeding through) or on the iPad the owner's daughter may be holding — at 4:3 a 49% window plus 45% ground either crops the void out of the window or pushes PLAY under the tab bar. The 12 push probes and the six lookbook views need a second and third aspect ratio in the contract.

NO CHILD-OBSERVED NUMBER: the owner reads numbers and the daughter is the tester, yet every acceptance bar is a machine bar (deltaE, px/frame, frame ratio). Nobody wrote the five-minute session protocol — time from cover-drop to her first PLAY tap, count of mis-taps on the diorama versus PLAY, whether she can say what the green dot wants without being read to — which is the only bar that answers 'does a six-year-old get it in the first second'.

THE RELOAD IS STILL THE UGLIEST MOMENT: a world switch, TAKE ME THERE and any cross-world replay remain a page reload (:6766-6770, :5518-5520) with the loader naming the world (:1687-1688); the 'next island as a locked jewel' reward on the end card is followed by a black boot cover and a cold rebuild. None of the three design the hand-off (holding the end-card poster as the cover art, or pre-warming the next world's assets while the end card is up) so the reward and the wait are the same picture.

THE WINDOW'S HIT-TEST IS UNDEFINED: 'tap the void to chomp' needs either a raycast against __voidGroup or a projected screen circle; 'tap anywhere in the window' (ONE ISLAND) and 'a tap on the void' (Splash Alive) are two different products for a child whose finger is 12 mm wide, and neither says what a tap on the landmark or the crowd does. This is also the mis-tap number the child protocol above should measure.
